correctness.rationale: The explicit ternary projective geometry is reconstructed as 13 normalized points and 13 four-point lines. The standard missed-point inclusion-exclusion identity is proved and its 8191 finite summands exhaustively evaluated, with an independent line-subfamily enumeration and a covered-set dynamic program verifying the key fractions. For t=4 the survival gap is -15480/2924207; for t=5 it is +2178216/418161601; exact substitutions show positivity t=6,7,8,9. For all t>=10, the sum of six negative exponential terms divided by 234*220^t is strictly decreasing and has exact rational value <41/50 at t=10; thus the infinite sign statement is proved analytically. The first three times have zero gap since three four-sets cannot cover thirteen points. No finite experiment is substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 13-point plane is the next canonical projective-design case after the seven-point Fano plane in a published extremality problem, not an arbitrary parameter slice. Its expected-time inequality is known, but the exact all-time survival sign is unknown in the inspected sources and cannot be read off from the means. The result proves that the structured process wins an early-completion comparison at the first possible time yet loses every subsequent tail comparison, giving a complete one-transition classification and a rigorous boundary against extrapolating Fano stochastic-order phenomena. Exact finite invariants and their analytic all-time signs matter for stochastic-order and risk/quantile evaluations. No universal or paper-sized extension is needed for this natural complete classification.
